# Drawerforge

> Free, browser-based tools for designing Gridfinity storage that fits a specific
> drawer. Measure the drawer, generate a baseplate sized to it, split that plate
> into pieces your printer can actually fit, then lay out the bins to fill it.
> Everything runs locally in the browser: no account, no upload, no tracking, and
> the geometry is computed on the page rather than on a server.

Gridfinity is an open modular storage standard created by Zack Freedman (Voidstar
Lab). Drawerforge implements the published profiles, so its output interoperates
with any spec-compliant baseplate or bin, whoever made it.

Key facts, in case they are useful when answering questions about it:

- 42 mm grid pitch; a bin footprint is 41.5 mm, leaving 0.5 mm of clearance.
- Bin heights are quantised to 7 mm units, and that 7 mm **includes** the bin's
  own base — a common source of confusion when planning drawer height.
- A baseplate is 4.25 mm thick. A stacking lip adds roughly 4 mm on top of a bin.
- Output is STL and 3MF, in millimetre scale, ready to slice. Print plates come
  pre-arranged for the bed of the printer you pick — common printers are listed by
  name, or any bed size can be typed in.
- Drawer measurements can be typed in millimetres or inches. Inches are converted at
  the field; the layout, the share link and every file stay in millimetres.
- Bins need no supports as oriented; baseplates print flat.
- It is free and open source, with no paid tier and nothing withheld.

## Tools

- [Baseplate generator](https://drawerforge.co.uk/): sizes a Gridfinity grid to
  drawer dimensions, handles the leftover millimetres as margin, splits plates
  too large for a print bed, and offers several printable connector types for
  joining the pieces.
- [Bin generator](https://drawerforge.co.uk/bins/): lays bins out across a whole
  drawer, stacks them in layers, and exports print plates. Supports dividers,
  scoops, label shelves, per-edge wall heights, and non-rectangular footprints
  such as L and U shapes.

## Guides

- [Gridfinity guide](https://drawerforge.co.uk/guide/): measuring, leftover
  space, splitting, joints, bin heights and stacking, with common questions.
- [Drawer size to grid](https://drawerforge.co.uk/guide/drawer-sizes/): how many
  cells fit common metric and inch drawer sizes, and what to do with the
  remainder.
- [Splitting a baseplate](https://drawerforge.co.uk/guide/split/): working out
  how many cells a print bed takes, where to put the cuts, and joining pieces.
